AIFIELD / AI WORKFLOWS

Assistance for the engineer. Review at every step.

AIFIELD’s supplied material explores agent-assisted engineering through command-line and Model Context Protocol (MCP) interactions. The described work is partial assistance; it does not establish autonomous end-to-end chip design.

HUMAN-CONTROLLED APPLICATION

The human review loop
01
Ask

The engineer describes a design task and its constraints.

02
Propose

An assistant prepares a candidate change or action.

03
Review & apply

A person inspects the proposal and controls its application.

04
Run & inspect

Tools execute the selected work; the engineer reviews results and limitations.

Engineering judgment stays visible

An assistant can help express a task and prepare actions, but a plausible proposal is not proof of a correct design. The engineer remains responsible for assumptions, setup, result interpretation and deciding whether further checks are required.

Before execution

Check the geometry, parameters and intended action.

After execution

Inspect results and compare against a suitable reference.

Local tools and external assistance

The context distinguishes local solver work from information that may be processed by an external assistant. The exact tool actions and data flow need current verification. No claim that every part of the workflow is local or confidential can be made from this material.

i

A demonstration should identify what information leaves the machine, the service receiving it and the person authorizing that step.

What to inspect in a demonstration

Ask to see a concrete task, the proposed action, the human intervention point, a solver result and a failure or limitation. A recorded sequence and available-action list would make the actual automation boundary reviewable.
